summary: Vaibhav Singh is a scholar of Indology and archaeology. He earned his PhD at the University of Reading by 2017, where he also held a post attested in 2018.
Valaiyattur Venkayya (1864–1912) was an Indology and archaeology scholar. He studied at Madras Christian College (~1881–1885) and the University of Madras (~1885–1887), and succeeded Eugen Hultzsch.

Valdo H. Viglielmo (1926–2016) was a scholar of Japanology and philosophy. Educated at Pennsylvania, Harvard, Tokyo, Gakushuin, and Meiji Gakuin, he taught at Meiji Gakuin, Harvard, and Princeton before serving as professor at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1965–2002).

Valeria Gazizova is a scholar in religious studies and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Oslo, completing a master's thesis under the supervision of Per Kværne, and was also taught by Hanna Havnevik.

Valerie Hansen (born 1958) is a historian and sinologist who studied under Victor H. Mair. She taught at East China Normal University (2005) and held posts at Yale University, including Professor of History attested between 1993 and 2018.

Van Austin Harvey (1926–2021) worked in religious studies and philosophy. Educated at Occidental, Princeton Theological Seminary, and Yale, he held posts at Princeton, Southern Methodist, Pennsylvania, and Stanford, where he was George Edwin Burnell Professor (~1978–1996).

Vans Kennedy (1784–1846) worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as judge-advocate-general for the Bombay Army (1817–1835) and held the presidency of both the Literary Society of Bombay and the Asiatic Society of Mumbai.

Vasant Shinde is a scholar of archaeology and Indology. He has served at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, where his appointments as professor include Professor of South Asian Archaeology attested in 2026.

Vasily Mikhaylovich Alekseyev (1881–1951) was a sinologist who studied at St. Petersburg University (~1898–1902) and under Édouard Chavannes (~1906–1909). He held long-term posts at Saint Petersburg State University (~1910–1951) and the Institute of Oriental Studies (~1918–1951).

Vasily Pavlovich Vasilyev (1818–1900) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Tibetology. Educated at Kazan Federal University under Józef Kowalewski, he became professor there in 1851 before serving as professor at Saint Petersburg State University from 1855.

Vasily Radlov (1837–1918) was a linguist and historian. Educated at Berlin and Jena, he taught in Barnaul before serving as director of the Asiatic Museum (1885–1890) and director of the Kunstkamera (1894–1918).

Vasily Seseman (1884–1963) was a philosopher who studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1903–1909). He held academic posts at Saint Petersburg State University (~1915–1918), Vytautas Magnus University (~1923–1940), and Vilnius University (~1940–1963).

Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale (1901–1991) was an Indologist, sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Bonn (1930). He held posts at Fergusson College, Visva-Bharati University, and the University of Delhi.

Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi (1893–1985) was an Indologist and historian educated at Deccan College and the University of Mumbai. He served as principal at Morris College and Vidarbha Institute, and was honorary professor at Rashtrasant Tukadoji Maharaj Nagpur University (1957–1966).

Vasudeva Sharan Agrawala (1904–1967) was an Indologist and archaeologist. Educated at Banaras Hindu University and the University of Lucknow, he served as curator of Mathura Museum, director of the State Museum, Lucknow, and head of Indology at BHU.

Vasudha Dalmia (born 1947) is an Indologist and historian educated at Miranda House, Cologne, JNU, and Heidelberg. She taught at the University of Tübingen and held the Magistretti Distinguished Professorship at the University of California, Berkeley (2001–2012).

Vasudha Narayanan (born 1953) is a scholar of religious studies and Indology with degrees from Madras, Mumbai, and Harvard. She served as Distinguished Professor of Religion at the University of Florida (~1982) and was president of the American Academy of Religion.

Vatroslav Jagić (1838–1923) was a linguist who studied at the University of Vienna (~1856–1860). He held academic posts at Odesa University, Humboldt University of Berlin, Imperial St. Petersburg University, and returned to the University of Vienna (~1886–1908).

Veeranarayana N. K. Pandurangi (born 1973) works in Indology and philosophy. Educated under Manikya Shastri and Martanda Dikshit, he held posts at Jagadguru Ramanandacharya Rajasthan Sanskrit University and served as Director of Research at Karnataka Samskrit University.

Velcheru Narayana Rao (born 1933) is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Sir C. R. Reddy College, Andhra University, and Osmania University, and served as Associate Professor of South Asian Studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison.
